clue.text: See 10
Takeaway republic?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: food '...', bought to eat elsewhere
second meaning: a West African country

explanation.walkthrough: Split as TO GO, the phrase is what you say when ordering food to carry out; run together it is a West African state.
explanation.definitionFit: Togo is a republic on the Gulf of Guinea, and 'to go' describes food ordered for carrying out.

clue.text: Slippery type of drug-runner

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a backless slipper or shoe
second meaning: a courier who smuggles drugs, often on the body

explanation.surface: A shifty character who smuggles narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slippery type' reads as a shifty person, but it means a type of slipper.
explanation.definitionFit: A mule is a backless slipper, and also slang for someone paid to carry illegal drugs across borders.

clue.text: Rotter with the Pied Piper's haul

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a nasty, contemptible person
second meaning, read as two words: a sack of rodents

explanation.surface: A scoundrel making off with the rodents the Pied Piper lured away.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pied Piper of Hamelin piped the town's rats away, so his haul would be a bag of rats.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratbag is informal slang for an unpleasant or despicable person, much like a rotter or a cad.

clue.text: A 10 1across affair?

parts.note: surface reading: an affair described by the phrase at 10 and 1 across, a cross-reference puzzle
setter's reading: a fling that is over by morning, a brief sexual encounter

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references fill in as 'here today, gone tomorrow', and an affair like that is a single night's encounter.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual sexual encounter lasting only one evening is exactly an affair here today and gone tomorrow.

clue.text: Right on time? No! Later, you ass!

parts.note: taken as written
an age is a period of time
R is the abbreviation for right; it does not come first but later, at the end

explanation.surface: Someone scolds a fool for being late rather than right on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right on time' reads in clue order, but 'No! Later' tells you to move the R to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An onager is a wild ass of central Asia, so the animal fits the insult used here.

clue.text: Hot type one cast into new type

indicators.note: metal cast into a mould takes a new shape, so these letters are melted down and reformed

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hot metal type is cast into a fresh typeface, a printing image.
explanation.walkthrough: The printing picture of hot metal type hides the abbreviation H for hot; the Greek roots neo and phyte mean new plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a beginner or recent convert, literally a new kind of person in a group.

clue.text: A lunar force returned to spread grass with gritty bits

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so these letters are read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
G is the symbol for gravitational force
to ted is to spread mown grass out to dry as hay

explanation.surface: A moon-powered force comes back to scatter grass that has grit in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first three pieces turn around; TED, a farming verb for tossing hay to dry, follows unreversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Granulated describes something formed into small grains, like sugar, so it has a gritty texture.

clue.text: Tory spin doctor's aim: a quarter of the revolution

parts.note: Tories are on the political right
a spin doctor's aim is to put an angle on a story

explanation.surface: A Conservative publicist hopes to win over part of a political uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' sounds political after Tory and spin doctor, but it is a full turn of 360 degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: A full turn is 360 degrees, and ninety degrees, one fourth of that circle, makes this angle.

clue.text: Flashers or gnashers

parts.note: surface reading: indecent exposers, a seedy picture
setter's reading: things that glint in a smile and are slang for teeth

explanation.walkthrough: Gnashers is British slang for teeth, and teeth made of a precious metal flash when their owner smiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental crowns of yellow metal both shine when someone grins and serve as chewing teeth.

clue.text: Right! One, two, three — go! Or may do otherwise, but not for long

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so these letters are arranged differently

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

parts.words: One, two, three — go! Or may do
parts.note: the words taken as written, punctuation dropped

explanation.surface: A starter counts down a race, and someone might set off otherwise, though only briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right!' looks like an exclamation of assent but supplies R to the twenty-one letter anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying describes something fleeting or transient, present one moment and vanished the next.

clue.text: Nora Batty to disembowel an ape?

indicators.note: batty means crazy, so this name is jumbled into a mad order

parts.note: taken as written
to gut a fish or animal is to remove its innards
taken as written

explanation.surface: The formidable Nora Batty threatens to gut a primate.
explanation.walkthrough: Nora Batty is a stout, fearsome housewife in the long-running British sitcom Last of the Summer Wine; her surname is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The orang-utan is a great ape with reddish hair living in the rainforests of Borneo and Sumatra.

clue.text: Parry's motivation: "Blame their failure on corruption!"

parts.note: to take the rap is to take the blame

indicators.note: a failure is a breakdown, so this word collapses and is rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written
rust is the corrosion or decay of metal

explanation.surface: A politician named Parry is spurred to blame others' failings on corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: Parry reads as a surname; in fencing a parry is the defensive block that a sword lunge provokes.
explanation.definitionFit: In fencing, an opponent's lunge with a slender sword is what prompts the defender's blocking move.

clue.text: Wren, familiarly say, angry when hatched

indicators.note: say asks us to go by how a name is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: the architect Sir Christopher Wren, called by his short name
cross means annoyed

explanation.surface: A little bird is cross when its eggs hatch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wren' looks like the bird, but it is the architect of St Paul's Cathedral, Christopher Wren.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatching is shading with lines, and criss-cross lines intersect in a crossing pattern.

clue.text: Range rider, callow out West, shot!

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so the remaining letters are scrambled
out means removed, so the compass point is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
W is the abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: An inexperienced cowboy in the Wild West is shot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Western picture of a callow rider being shot hides both a deletion and an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordillera is a chain of mountains, such as the Andes, so it is a mountain range.

clue.text: Tumult raised at abattoir's closure

indicators.note: raised means lifted upwards, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
the closure of a word is its ending, so the letters are taken from its tail

parts.note: the last four letters of abattoir

explanation.surface: An uproar breaks out when a slaughterhouse is shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closure' sounds like the abattoir being shut, but it means the end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A riot is a violent public disturbance, a tumult of uproar and disorder.

clue.text: Executed, having attempted the murder of Eos

definitions.meaning: first meaning: put to death by firing squad at first light
second meaning: fired a gun at the Greek goddess of daybreak

explanation.surface: Someone is put to death for trying to kill a Greek goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: Eos is the Greek goddess of the dawn, so trying to kill her is firing at Dawn, read as a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserters were traditionally killed by firing squad at first light, and firing on a goddess is attempted murder.

clue.text: Rich worker attached to a German union

parts.note: taken as written
Bund is the German word for a union or federation
a worker ant

explanation.surface: A wealthy labourer has joined a German trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: Worker is the crossword's usual ant (or bee); here it comes last in the answer though first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich in the sense of plentiful or copious, as in a rich harvest, matches abundant.

clue.text: "Singin' a song ____", in concert

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the missing words of the old popular song '...'

explanation.surface: A singalong lyric performed at a live show.
explanation.walkthrough: The song runs 'we'll travel along, singin' a song, side by side'; 'in concert' looks musical but means together.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in concert means acting together alongside one another, adjacent and cooperating.

clue.text: Any Bront? sister roped into service?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the shared pen-name surname of Charlotte, Emily and Anne
second meaning: something pulled on a rope to call people to church

explanation.surface: One of the Brontë sisters is dragooned into helping.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brontës published as Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell; a church bell is rung with a rope to summon worshippers to a service.
explanation.definitionFit: The sisters shared one pseudonymous surname, and a church peal is sounded by pulling ropes before worship.

clue.text: Party colours worn with grace?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a rosette or ribbon worn to show allegiance

explanation.surface: Someone wears party colours gracefully.
explanation.walkthrough: A favour here is a badge, rosette or ribbon worn to show support for a party or side.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in someone's good graces is to have their approval; a rosette of ribbons is also so called.

clue.text: Some time since Julian Clary neared a disaster

indicators.note: a disaster is a wreck, so these letters lie scattered in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Comedian Julian Clary has been close to catastrophe for a while now.
explanation.walkthrough: Julian Clary is a camp British comedian, but Julian here points to Julius Caesar's calendar, which set the year at 365 days.
explanation.definitionFit: The year of January to December is a period reckoned on the modern calendar, descended from the Roman one.

clue.text: Oil producer a friend to many

parts.note: a pal is a friend
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, which is many

explanation.surface: An oil company is generous to many people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil producer' suggests a company or a country; it is a tree, the oil palm.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil palms bear fruit whose pulp and kernels are pressed for palm oil, so the tree yields oil.

clue.text: See 11
Here Caruso arrived at work on time

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: The tenor Caruso turned up punctually for his job.
explanation.walkthrough: Enrico Caruso was the great Italian tenor, so the place he arrived, meaning made his name, is the stage of musical drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Italian tenor made his reputation and fame singing sung drama on stage.

clue.text: Preparation against the offensive

parts.note: surface reading: military readiness for an enemy attack
setter's reading: a cosmetic product applied to prevent body odour

explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' is a military attack in the surface but an unpleasant smell in the answer; 'preparation' is a substance prepared for use.
explanation.definitionFit: This toiletry is applied to the skin to mask or prevent unpleasant sweat smells.

clue.text: Austerity city lets one knock back a gin on Sunday

indicators.note: to knock back is to drink, but also to send backwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
a gin is a snare for catching animals
S is the abbreviation for Sunday

explanation.surface: A frugal town allows a drink of gin on the Sabbath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock back a gin' reads as drinking; gin is the old word for a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek city was famous for its harsh, frugal discipline, the origin of the adjective spartan.

clue.text: He's paid to make bank transfers

definitions.text: He's paid to make bank transfers

parts.words: He's paid to make bank transfers
parts.note: surface reading: a bank clerk who moves money between accounts

parts.words: He's paid to make bank transfers
parts.note: setter's reading: a boatman who carries people from one river bank to the other

explanation.walkthrough: The bank is a riverbank, not a financial one, and the transfers are passengers carried across the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatman who carries passengers across a river for a fare moves them between its two shores.
